thread:
maria: heads-up — noticed weird memory blowups on continuous batching when lots of short sequences land in the same batch. not full OOM but large padding spikes and a couple of worker restarts. attaching quick profiler snapshot and observations. :thinking:

sam: can you paste the profiler output? is this the kv cache evict storm we saw last week?

maria: not exactly kv evict storm. this looks like per-seq margin allocation generating small temporary workspaces for each short seq; when batch grows the allocator keeps handing out new tail buffers instead of reusing a small slab. padding overhead jumps.

jordan: interesting — are you seeing this only with kernel-switch enabled? could be kernel's per-request scratch size estimation is bigger for some kernels and triggers workspace splits.

maria: yes, 2x more frequent when kernel-switch picks the fused-attn kernel. here's the short output from the perf harness (cut):

```
batch_size=64 seq_len_dist=mix(short=0.7,long=0.3)
memory: baseline=24.1GB used=21.8GB peak=23.5GB
padding_waste: 12% -> 28% after growth
workspace_allocs: tail_slab_hits=38% tail_slab_misses=62%
kv_cache_pressure: hit_rate=0.94 but footprint spikes on batch join
oom_events: 2 (soft-restart)
```

lee: that tail_slab_miss rate is the problem. allocator frag + per-seq margin rounding is burning small regions. we should consider a reuse path for micro-tail allocations.

sam: what about proactive coalescing? when batch grows from N->N+M, precompute expected seq length histogram, reserve one larger workspace and give references instead of new allocations. reduces allocator churn.

jordan: risk is over-reserving and increasing latency for long sequences. but we can make it adaptive: only coalesce for groups where average seq_len < threshold and kernel expected scratch < X. we can also bias kernel selection to the smaller-scratch variant for those groups.

maria: sketch of heuristic I prototyped: if short_seq_ratio > 0.6 AND expected_batch_growth > 10% then enable micro-reuse mode: allocate shared_tail_slab sized to max_short_seq_scratch and hand out offsets. fallback when long seq arrives. so far reduces padding_waste to ~9% in the harness.

sam: nice. any changes to KV cache behavior? prefetching can increase footprint and interact badly with reuse if we pin pages.

maria: I added a conservative prefetch hint: only prefetch for requests that are expected to run the same kernel variant and have cache_hot_score > 0.8. that keeps kv footprint stable. results: kv footprint spike down 40%.

lee: couple implementation notes: 1) need to tighten our workspace lifetime so reuse doesn't race with async kernel calls; use an ownership token on the offset reference. 2) update telemetry to emit tail_slab_miss metric per-batch.

jordan: also add a kernel-selection cost function term for reuse friendliness (penalize kernels that need large per-request scratch). should be small change in selection logic.

opsbot: perf-harness/2005001234 triggered: job queued, tags=[continuous-batch,reuse-probe].

sam: can you open a short PR with the heuristic and a flag? i'd like to try this on dedicated infra. name it `adaptive_tail_reuse` behind runtime config.

maria: will do. I'll add tests that simulate rapid batch growth and a mixed seq distribution. also add a small fuzz test for race with async kernels.

lee: one more thought — for extremely short sequences we might keep a tiny shared pool that never gets returned to global allocator (leaked-on-purpose) up to a cap; fast path to avoid lock churn. but need to monitor cumulative cap closely. :warning:

jordan: agree, but keep it an opt-in telemetry-only experiment first. want to correlate memory cap vs latency.

maria: plan: PR today with flag + telemetry, run canaries on dedicated + hosted small fleet. i'll post results. thanks all :thumbsup:
